text.p: Manchester United striker Eric Cantona is retiring from professional soccer, the club announced on Sunday.
The decision by the 30-year-old French international was announced at a news conference at United's Old Trafford ground by club chairman Martin Edwards.
Cantona, who will be 31 on May 24, has had a moderate season for United, although the club retained the English premier league title -- their fourth league triumph in five seasons.
The Frenchman has had a colourful history in his years with United, most famously in 1995 when he took a flying kick at a Crystal Palace fan and ended up in court.
He helped Leeds to the premier league championship in 1992 before leaving 10 months later for Manchester United with whom he has won four championship medals.
Before leaving France, Cantona played for Auxerre, Martigues, Marseille, Bordeaux, Montpellier and Nimes.
